A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EffGen, with the same authors, core framework and principal benchmark study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching extensively relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, component ablations, timing measurements and error analyses in Tables 2–3 and multiple appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional controls, ablations, sensitivity tests and SWE-Bench Lite evaluation.

M1.justification: v2 adds native/hybrid tool-calling strategies, provider-policy routing, guardrails and a RAG pipeline. Reported core procedures also change: Jaccard-based deduplication becomes consecutive normalized equality, and LLM-based memory summarization becomes heuristic summarization. These are substantial procedural revisions, beyond the expanded tool inventory and implementation documentation.

E1.justification: The original 13-benchmark coverage remains, while v2 Appendix W.3 adds SWE-Bench Lite evaluation on 300 repository-repair instances. Repository-level, multi-file software repair substantially extends the task requirements beyond the existing algorithmic code-execution benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 adds Raw+Search to the SimpleQA comparison, retaining Raw Model, LangChain, AutoGen and Smolagents. It also removes the numerical manual-validation and schema-only comparisons from v1 Appendix I.5. Reactive routing was already a comparator in v1; its expanded documentation does not establish a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 replaces category-specific 1–10-minute timeouts with five minutes throughout Table 50. Its reproducibility tables reconcile previously conflicting sample counts and stop sequences, including GSM8K's 1,319 versus 500 examples. New SWE-Bench and sensitivity protocols and revised microbenchmark hardware/workloads further change evaluation settings. These reporting revisions do not establish that retained benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix W adds a tool-access control, Gemma component ablations, domain-specific threshold sensitivity, nested-call overhead analysis, long-horizon memory stress tests, per-technique prompt ablations and routing-weight sensitivity. Conversely, several earlier systems analyses, including protocol microbenchmarks and parallel-orchestration scaling measurements, are removed.

E5.justification: v2 removes v1 Table 69's statement about three-seed results with 95% confidence intervals and qualifies blanket uncertainty/significance claims. Revised memory/tool measurements report p50/p95 and sample counts; weight sensitivity reports variation across ten random weight settings. The binomial-interval convention, McNemar testing and listed seed 42 remain. Removed reporting does not establish fewer actual runs.

E6.justification: Tables 63–70 add substantial new results, including Raw+Search accuracies and SWE-Bench Lite outcomes. Table 2 corrects AutoGen's 1.5B average from 34.33 to 33.57 while retaining its individual scores. Error totals change from 500 to 600 with unchanged category counts and corrected percentages. Numerous systems measurements are also removed or replaced under different conditions.

T1.justification: Formal specifications are substantially revised across components: duplicate detection changes mathematically, requirement counting gains a floor and different indicators, memory scoring is replaced by a different consolidation formula, and GPU memory/allocation equations are rewritten. The FAISS-IVF search-complexity derivation is removed. These alter mathematical definitions and reasoning rather than merely notation.

C1.justification: The principal SLM framework contributions and complementary-scaling claims remain. The abstract narrows unconditional 70–80% context compression to input-prompt compression of up to 70–80%, with 57% average reduction. The headline 1.5B advantage is also corrected from 13.1 to 13.2 percentage points following the baseline-average correction.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the erroneous synergistic-ablation interpretation with overlapping component contributions. It adds tool-access attribution, cross-family generalization discussion and repository-coding limitations. Applicability qualifications also change substantially: memory encryption/access controls are explicitly unimplemented, large-scale latency claims are qualified, and the contribution is characterized as an engineered integration of established ideas.

D1.justification: v2 documents release v0.2.10, expanded backends/tools, production subsystems, revised APIs and dependencies, and new measurement details. Extensive installation, configuration and example code is replaced by external documentation pointers. The stated license changes from MIT to Apache 2.0. Appendix Y.7 changes current code availability to a future-release promise, conflicting with availability statements elsewhere in v2.

R1.justification: The broad related-work positioning remains, but v2 removes several citations, including Lewis et al.'s retrieval-augmented generation and Taori et al.'s Alpaca, and replaces the TPTU citation with TPTU-v2. It also withdraws the appendix's first-unified-implementation wording and more explicitly positions the contribution as SLM-specific integration.

P1.justification: Appendices are extensively reorganized around architecture, components, infrastructure and experiments. The former usage guide and agent examples become condensed material in Appendix X, while many technical passages and operational walkthroughs are rewritten. v2 also adds an appendix roadmap, conflict disclosure and impact statement; this exceeds routine language polishing.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantially resized and relocated displays. Appendix tables are added, removed and redesigned, including tool inventories, replacement latency tables and extended-analysis tables. The session-lifecycle figure disappears, while a new accuracy-scaling figure redisplays retained Qwen results.

improvement.justification: The Raw+Search control and Gemma ablations strengthen attribution and generalization, while corrected averages, error totals and ablation interpretation improve accuracy. These benefits are tempered by unresolved main-text/appendix disagreements about procedures, such as sentence splitting and memory scoring. Reproduction documentation also becomes less self-contained, and the future-release statement conflicts with current-availability claims. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
